newsitem.title: UK: Rentokil sees five pct sterling hit.
newsitem.headline: Rentokil sees five pct sterling hit.

text.p: Business services group Rentokil Initial Plc said on Wednesday that its 1997 pre-tax profit would be reduced by around five percent if sterling continued at current levels.
Chief executive Sir Clive Thompson told a news conference that the rise of sterling at the end of 1996 had reduced last year's sales by 15.4 million pounds and pre-tax profits by 3.2 million pounds.
Thompson also said that the exceptional charge for restructuring the business related to last year's acquisition of BET would be "double digit millions but not as high as 16 million stg".
The company took an exceptional charge of 16.4 million stg against 1996 earnings which included almost 1.5 million stg paid to former BET chief executive John Clark.
Thompson said that the two-for-one share split announced earlier on Wednesday would take effect on May 16, if shareholders approved the move.
